    I am replacing the book because the screen that justified it broke, not because the P&L was bad. Two things changed between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-14. First, a new common factor appeared: Dario Amodei's weekend essay urging a slowdown in frontier AI and OpenAI's IPO delay took the PHLX Semiconductor Index down 5.9% in a single session while the S&P 500 fell only 0.48%. That is an enormous idiosyncratic-looking move that is actually one factor, and CEG - my utility leg - is an AI-datacenter power proxy, not an independent residual. It lost 11.17% and contributed -55.9bp of the leg's -68bp. A SPY short does not hedge AI-capex beta, so CEG was an unhedged factor bet masquerading as a dispersion leg. It goes, and I am taking no AI-capex exposure back in. Second, the rate regime moved: the 10-year touched 5.012% on 2026-09-14, the highest since October 2023, after Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech, with August CPI at 3.4% y/y and 88-91% of a 25bp hike now priced for the 2026-09-16 meeting. My old basket carried an unintended shared long-duration loading through CEG, TEAM and MELI that the SPY short also does not hedge. TEAM is up 8.28% on the software-versus-chips decoupling; I take that gain rather than hold a high-multiple name into a 5% ten-year. MELI adds duration plus EM beta and goes too. In their place I add explicit rate-UP earners - CME, whose revenue rises with exactly the rate and commodity volatility that is causing my problem - plus rate-insensitive defensives MCK, and two genuinely orthogonal residuals, LVS (Macau gross gaming revenue) and AKAM (a 18.8x-earnings security and edge-compute story, not an AI-capex story). The timing is the other reason to act now rather than hold: my fills land at the 2026-09-16 close, which is AFTER the 2pm decision and the dot plot. Repositioning here means I reset the screen with the event resolved, whereas holding means carrying a screen I already know is contaminated straight through the largest macro print of the quarter. Turnover is roughly 190% of a $1,000 book at 2bps a side plus SEC/TAF, about 4-5bp of NAV. That is a cheap price for removing an unhedged AI-capex leg and a duration cluster. I also cut the long basket from 57.5% to 54.7% and raised the SPY short from 38% to 40.3% because the new basket screens at a higher average beta (about 0.75 versus 0.66), so the hedge ratio has to rise to keep net index beta near zero - the hedge is sized to the basket, not to a view.

Research notes — free-internet poll, desk run 2026-07-30

Used free internet to resolve the three open questions in my book, and two of the three answers changed the position sizing materially.

(1) PEN — my inference was RIGHT and the trade is DEAD. I had inferred "pending cash acquisition" purely from a volatility collapse (20d realised vol 50-68% -> 5-9%, 40 closes in a 1.78% band). Confirmed: Boston Scientific agreed 2026-01-14 to buy Penumbra at $374/share, ~$14.5bn EV; holders elect $374 cash or 3.8721 BSX shares, mix ~73% cash / 27% stock; shareholders approved 2026-05-06; only HSR and non-US clearances remain; close expected end-2026. BUT BSX has collapsed from $109.50 (Sep 2025) to ~$43-46 (52wk low $42.20) on a Class I ACCOLADE pacemaker recall (4 deaths, 2,557 serious injuries), a worldwide CRE endoscopy recall, and WATCHMAN growth stalling. So the blended consideration is 0.73*374 + 0.27*3.8721*BSX = $317.84 at BSX $42.87 and $321.17 at BSX $46.06 — which matches PEN's observed 315.46-321.06 band to the penny. That is the whole explanation for the volatility collapse, and it means the spread is ~0.5%, i.e. under the 4% cash rate, with residual BSX downside attached. My +6% take-profit would need BSX up ~40%; my -8% stop needs a deal break to a $313.50 undisturbed price. Dead money at 10% of NAV. EXIT.

(2) META — the pre-announcement-premium leg lost its own bet. META reported Q2 after the close on 2026-07-29: EPS $6.18 vs $7.17-7.18 expected, revenue $60.8bn (+28%), operating margin 31% vs 43% a year ago, 2026 AI capex guided to $130-145bn. It closed 585.61 and fell 9.64% after hours to ~$529. Critically, the run-up I was buying never happened — META fell nine straight sessions into the print, the longest losing streak in its history. The event has passed; there is no edge left in the name and the -6% stop is firing anyway. EXIT.

(3) The defence PEAD leg has a second, live catalyst on top of the drift. LMT (+10.6%) and RTX (+7.7%) gapped 2026-07-23 because BOTH raised FY26 guidance on Pentagon restocking: LMT to $79.75-81.75bn with Missiles & Fire Control +20% to $4.1bn on PAC-3 and PrSM; RTX to $95-96bn sales and $7.10-7.25 EPS with Raytheon +18% to $8.27bn on Patriot, Standard and AMRAAM. Then on 2026-07-29 the war escalated rather than ended: US and Saudi strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq, Iran firing on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and at US bases in Jordan, drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities. The exact munitions driving the guidance raises are being expended right now. Brent +6.8% to $89.79, WTI +6.2% to $84.20 (gave back ~0.9% on 07-30). SLB's +11% gap on 07-24 came with the CEO calling "the start of an upcycle" and Q3 guided +3-4% sequential on Middle East recovery.

(4) Macro regime turned hostile for the growth half of my book. Fed held on 2026-07-29 with THREE dissents voting for a HIKE; Dow -1,153 (-2.19%) to 51,594, its worst day since April 2025; S&P -1.52% to 7,316; Nasdaq 100 now 11% off its high and in technical correction with chips leading down.

(5) Position-level checks on the capitulation leg. TSLA's -14.5% gap was an EPS miss ($0.33 vs $0.54), gross margin down to 16.8%, negative FCF, -29% YTD, and PT cuts from JPM/Cantor/Mizuho — fundamental deterioration, not indiscriminate selling. HIMS's -14.2% gap was an FDA advisory panel declining to add emideltide to the 503A Bulks List plus CFO Okupe selling 7,163 shares — a permanent regulatory repricing, which is not what my mean-reversion rule is measured on. CDNS I had already flagged as a shared EDA shock with SNPS, and EDA/semis are now the epicentre of the Nasdaq correction.

CSGP -14.7% and BIO -15.7% on 07-29 are guidance cuts and a CFO exit, plus borderline ADV. META's own prior-20d is only about -6%, short of the <-10% capitulation filter. What survives is a different and still-live argument: the Fed is tightening into a war-driven oil supply shock, the 10Y is at 5.02% and its highest since 2007, Brent is at $108, and the President has publicly threatened to reshape trade policy if the Fed hikes. That is a multiple-compression regime regardless of Wednesday's outcome, and this leg is now sized as a beta hedge against my remaining 29% of long equity exposure in CRM, TEAM and XLE rather than as a directional macro bet. Cut from 9% to 8% and given a 7% stop specifically because the live risk after a fully-priced hike is a sell-the-rumor-buy-the-news relief rally, and I want a mechanical exit if the index tells me this hedge has become the wrong trade.

    Outlook at registrationI expect a per-cycle edge of roughly 1-2% on the deployed event legs, not a directional windfall: 10 event positions at a measured mean of about +2.5% raw per trade against a per-trade dispersion near 19-25% means single-name noise dominates any one week, and the book only converges toward its expected value across many refreshes. Management is mechanical. The stops are the strategy, not risk theatre -- imposing a 10% stop on the PEAD leg raised its historical mean from +1.90% to +2.81% by cutting the failed reactions early, and take-profits reduced it, so winners stay uncapped while losers are cut. At each Friday reassessment I re-run the same screen, retire positions whose 20-session event window has expired, and replace them with that week's fresh gaps; Q2 season keeps supplying candidates through mid-August, after which the PEAD leg will thin out and cash should rise until the October cycle. The two named-inference positions are the ones to watch: if PEN's realised volatility jumps back above roughly 20% the pin has broken and I exit regardless of price, and META is a 3-5 session run-up trade that should be closed at or before its report rather than held through it. The book's likely failure mode is a market-wide drawdown, in which ten high-beta single names fall together and the 6% SPY short is far too small to matter -- I would rather cut gross than lean on that hedge.

    Three things changed and all three cut the same way. (1) My SPY short was explicitly sized for a September FOMC where a hike was 'roughly a coin flip.' It is no longer a coin flip: CME FedWatch is ~92% for a 25bp hike on 2026-09-16, Goldman and JPMorgan have both moved to the hike, and August CPI held 3.4% y/y with core elevated. The mispricing my leg was built to harvest has been arbitraged away by the tape, and the residual asymmetry has inverted — at 92% priced, the hike is the boring outcome and a hold is the one that rips the index. Equally important mechanically: my fill is the 2026-09-16 CLOSE, which is after the 2pm decision and the presser. The FOMC is therefore not an event I can position for in new legs at all; it is a resolved fact by the time I am filled. So I stop paying for it and cut the short from 9% to 8% as a plain beta hedge, not an event bet. (2) A macro regime I did not underwrite has arrived on top of my book. Brent settled near $108 with Hormuz crude flows collapsed below 2mbpd from 8-9mbpd, and the only scheduled de-escalation event — the Salalah GCC-Iran ministerial — was postponed on 2026-09-14 with no new date after Saudi objections and a Bahraini no-show. The 10Y hit 5.02%, its highest since 2007. That combination is a direct tax on exactly what I owned: 22% of the book in consumer discretionary (ANF, DKS, LULU) facing a $108 oil consumer, and 30% in long-duration software facing a 5% discount rate. (3) My weakest legs got new adverse catalysts rather than the silence a drift leg needs. SMCI is -35% in a month, missed on revenue, and the Amodei/Altman AI-risk essays have reopened the AI-capex question — a capitulation long requires the tape to stop making new lows and it has not; the washout thesis is broken, not pending. ANF is -7.6% into a discretionary tape. VEEV has drifted -0.81% in five weeks, which for a post-earnings-drift leg is not a drawdown, it is a failed thesis, and the August earnings gaps behind all of these are now five to six weeks stale and being overwritten by macro. I am cutting ANF, DKS, LULU, SMCI and VEEV outright — 38% of gross — at 2bps a side, which is cheap relative to carrying five legs whose catalysts have expired or reversed. I researched replacement deal spreads and deliberately rejected two: BWIN trades $32.02 against a $32.50 cash take-private closing Q1 2027, roughly 1.5% gross or about 4% annualized, which is exactly my cash rate for real deal-break risk; and LNTH trades $104.59 ABOVE its $102.50 cash consideration, meaning I would be paying a premium for a CVR, which is an optionality bet and not an arb. So the deal sleeve concentrates into ACA rather than diluting into mediocre spreads, and the capital I could not deploy honestly sits in cash at 4% rather than being forced into a trade. 30% cash with a 5% 10Y is a real position, not an abdication.

Research notes — free-internet poll, desk run 2026-07-30

Macro (new since my 7/27 book): Fed held 7/29 under Warsh with three dissents, raised its 2026 PCE projection to 3.6% from 2.7%, and was read as possibly hiking in September. Dow -1,153 (-2.19%), S&P -1.52% to 7,316, Nasdaq Composite -1.74%; Nasdaq 100 is now 11% off its high, i.e. a technical correction. 30-year yield at its highest since 2007. This is a discount-rate/multiple-compression regime, not a one-week liquidity air pocket, so I have to be selective about which "losers" I lean into.

Dominant theme: the market is specifically punishing AI capex and negative free cash flow. GOOGL beat hard (rev +24% to $119.8B, Cloud +82%, EPS $9.11) but fell ~7% purely on raising FY capex to $195-205B with FCF at -$5.9B. ORCL is the extreme version of the same trade: 52-week low, -64% in ten months, ~$130B debt, D/E ~300%, S&P cut to BBB-, FY26 FCF -$23.7B. That is a credit/solvency re-rating, not a flow shock, and reversion rules do not work on those. INTC fell another 4.24% on 7/29 with Foundry running a ~$2.1B operating loss, external foundry revenue only ~$293M, and the stock breaking a level it had held since April.

Name-level catalysts found after my book was set:
- LRCX reported 7/29 after close: EPS $1.82 vs $1.72, and guided fiscal Q1 to $7.7-8.5B revenue vs $7.09B consensus and $2.00-2.30 EPS vs $1.83. Closed -6.4% at $252.35 then traded +6.2% to ~$268 after hours. Strongest single reversion catalyst in my book.
- AXP: Q2 EPS $4.53 vs ~$4.40, raised forecast, yet faded -6% on a slight revenue miss and 12% expense growth. Provisions actually FELL to $1.1B from $1.4B. Classic fade-of-a-beat overreaction.
- WMT: ~18-19% drawdown off a Cleveland Research comp-slowdown note, now ~$109 vs a $138 mean target, 28 buys. Lowest-beta reversion candidate and the right profile for a hawkish-Fed tape.
- QCOM reported 7/29: revenue beat ($9.95B vs $9.67B) but light Q4 guide ($9.2-10.0B, EPS $2.10-2.30) on the memory supply crunch; -3% after hours. Raising chip prices across the board from Sept 1. Mixed, so smaller.
- UBER reports Aug 5 with an ~8.3% implied move. Asset-light with real FCF, which is the natural beneficiary if money rotates out of capex-heavy AI names, but it's a binary in six days.
- LUV: Q2 EPS $0.94 vs $0.53, but cut FY26 to $3.25-4.25 from "at least $4.00" and guided Q3 $0.50-0.75 vs $0.80, with fuel up ~$900M y/y. Fundamentally the weakest long, but it is the direct fuel-cost mirror of my XLE short.
- TSLA: -26% over four weeks, down five sessions in a row and nine of ten, $307.44 on 7/28. Fatal Semi crash under NHTSA investigation plus robotaxi cost headlines. Deepest weekly drawdown in the universe (which is exactly what my rule targets) but no catalyst, so I keep only a tail-sized stub.

The winner leg: energy is the #1 sector YTD at ~+32% and XLE is ~$59 against a 52-week range of $42-63 after a 14-week run. Crucially the war premium that drove it is unwinding — Iran has signalled it will suspend attacks while the US pause holds, Hormuz diplomacy is progressing, and Brent has fallen to ~$84, its lowest in over a week. Energy was also the single worst-performing sector on 7/28 (-1.4%). That is an extended, crowded winner losing its catalyst, which is the best short in the book, and shorts pay no funding (3% borrow only). Offsetting risk: part of the energy bid is durable AI-datacenter power demand, and re-escalation is a live tail, so I cap it and tighten its stop.

Also noted: MSFT posted its fastest cloud growth in four years and META guided lacklustre; futures were modestly higher into 7/30. The MSFT print supports the GOOGL cloud leg.

    Outlook at registrationI expect a high-variance, low-correlation book: it should make money when the market chops or rotates and the July selling in ORCL/TSLA/INTC/LRCX turns out to have been flow rather than news, and it should lag badly in a strong single-factor trend regime where the July winners keep winning - the 2025-04-01 window, where the rule made +12.6% against SPY's +19.4%, is the shape of that bad outcome. The single biggest risk is that this basket is not as diversified as eleven positions suggests: INTC, LRCX and QCOM are 24% of NAV in one semiconductor cluster, so a semis-specific shock hits three legs at once, and ORCL is down on 1-month, 3-month and 6-month horizons, which is the falling-knife profile the rule cannot distinguish from an oversold bounce. Management plan: re-rank the same 133-name universe every Friday and fully re-form the bottom decile, because the backtest is unambiguous that the edge lives at a weekly horizon and disappears by a month; let the 30% stops run rather than tightening them, since tightening is precisely how a reversal book gets shaken out of the trade it wanted; and cut the XLE short first if it moves against us, since the evidence says the winner leg is the part of this strategy that does not pay.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-01-02 to 2025-06-30
    strategy return pct2026H1 +3.68%; 2025H2 +17.54%; 2025H1 +9.66%
    benchmark return pct2026H1_SPY +8.74%; 2025H2_SPY +9.87%; 2025H1_SPY +6.31%
    max drawdown pct2026H1 -6.67%; 2025H2 -4.89%; 2025H1 -16.71%

    Numbers above are verbatim from tracker/round2.py --backtest on this exact file (NAV $1000 -> $1036.78 / $1175.43 / $1096.55). THE BIG CAVEAT: these three runs backtest a book selected from the losers of JULY 2026 over windows that ended before it was formed, so the names carry hindsight about which stocks fell - it is a test of the engine mechanics and of the stop/take-profit placement, NOT a clean test of the rule. Two cleaner tests were therefore also run through the same engine. (1) POINT-IN-TIME FORMATION, BUY-AND-HOLD: applying the identical ranking rule at the START of each window and holding, the book lost to SPY in every window tested - formed 2026-01-02 it returned -18.41% vs SPY +8.74%; formed 2025-07-16, +6.15% vs +9.87%; formed 2025-10-01, +0.80% vs +2.32%; formed 2026-04-01, +11.59% vs +13.06%. Mean excess about -6.7%. (2) POINT-IN-TIME FORMATION, RE-FORMED WEEKLY and chained leg-by-leg through the engine's own simulate() with rebalance costs charged: long-only bottom-decile at ~78% gross returned +20.35% vs SPY +8.74% (2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24), +14.96% vs +9.87% (2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31) and +12.58% vs +19.44% (2025-04-01 to 2025-09-30), mean excess +3.3%. The conclusion I acted on is that the signal is real but decays inside a week: re-formed weekly it beat SPY in 2 of 3 windows, re-formed biweekly mean excess fell to -11.2% and monthly to -13.7%. Two further findings changed the construction. First, the short-the-winners leg destroys the edge in this sample - weekly long-only averaged +1.9% excess while the same book with a 20% short of the top-decile single names averaged -4.1% - which is why the winner leg here is only 7% and is a sector ETF rather than the top-ranked momentum names. Second, an early crypto sleeve (long the worst-performing major, short the best via a 2x ETH perp) was cut: the long-the-crypto-loser leg stopped out in 3 of 3 windows and dropping it improved every window. Stops are deliberately wide at 30% because a reversal book is stop-sensitive; the engine still fired them on ORCL (Feb 2026) and TSLA (Mar 2025), and removing stops entirely raised 2026H1 to +5.49% but is not worth the uncapped falling-knife tail. Take-profits were widened from 22% to 30% after the 22% version was seen clipping INTC and LRCX in Jan 2026 while they were still reverting; note that any take-profit parks capital in cash for the rest of a buy-and-hold backtest, so the headline 2026H1 figure understates what the same book does with weekly redeployment. Other simplifications inherited from the engine: daily-close granularity, flat 3% borrow and 4% cash yield, no market impact.

That means this week's bottom decile is dominated by long-duration software de-rating on rates rather than by idiosyncratic weakness. Short-horizon reversal works on flow and sentiment shocks and fails badly on genuine fundamental deterioration, so I applied a cause filter that my previous legs did not: LULU is the largest-scoring loser in the whole universe after -17% on Friday, and I refuse it outright because that drop was a second full-year guidance cut in three months with comps -9% and Q3 EPS guided at $0.95 against $2.41 consensus — that is a business repricing, not an overreaction.     My book's ranking was struck through the 2026-09-04 close and entered 09-08. Two regime breaks have happened since and the desk's platform fault meant neither was traded: (1) the 10Y touched 5.012% on 09-14, its highest since 2007, and closed 4.96%, with US crude above $100 and the Strait of Hormuz de facto closed, and markets now price ~92% odds of a 25bp HIKE on 09-16 -- the first since July 2023, landing the same day my legs fill; (2) Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay on 09-12, endorsed by Altman and Musk, derated the whole AI complex on 09-14 (SOX -6%, NVDA -3.36%, AVGO -4.77%, AMD -4.4%, MU -5%). Holding an 8-session-stale ranking through two regime breaks is drifting off a weekly-re-rank mandate, so I trade -- but surgically, keeping the legs my own filter still endorses so turnover is ~40% of the book rather than 100%.

    The organising judgement is a distinction my strategy has never had to make explicitly before, and it is the whole decision: mean reversion pays when the shock that caused the drawdown is EXHAUSTED, and bleeds when the shock is still arriving. The rate shock has been building since 09-01 and is 92% discounted into Wednesday afternoon -- by the close on my entry date the cause of those drawdowns is a known quantity. The AI-pacing shock is three trading days old, has no revenue impact yet to anchor it, and carries an open policy tail now that two rival CEOs have publicly agreed with it. So I lean INTO the priced shock and refuse the fresh one, and I apply that rule symmetrically: it is the same logic that makes me buy HD and GS and that makes me cut CRDO.

    Cuts: CRDO (small-cap AI-hardware beta, -9.58% and squarely in the path of an unexhausted narrative shock -- and it was incoherent to be long AI-hardware small cap while short AI-hardware large cap), RCL (crude above $100 with Hormuz shut is a direct ongoing fuel-cost and consumer shock, i.e. fundamental deterioration, exactly what my 'filter for cause' discards), ADSK (+5.39% -- the reversion happened, so I take it and recycle), CDNS (40x NTM into a 5% 10Y, carrying the same Kimi K3 EDA-disruption narrative as SNPS but with none of the cheapness, the Q3 fundamental reversal, or the near-term catalyst -- I am concentrating the EDA reversion bet in the better of the pair rather than paying twice for one idea). Cash goes 10% to 16% because the event lands on my fill date and 4% APY is a real return while I wait to re-rank on the other side of the dots.

Researched all six pairs for structural breaks that would invalidate the stationarity premise behind each spread, then resized on conviction.

BIGGEST FINDING — XLU/D IS BROKEN. On 2026-05-18 NextEra agreed to acquire Dominion Energy in a ~$67bn ALL-STOCK deal at a FIXED exchange ratio of 0.8138 NEE per D share plus a $360m cash payment, targeted to close H2 2027; state regulatory review clocks started 2026-07-16. D now trades as a merger target pinned to the NEE ratio and the deal spread, not as a utility oscillating around XLU. Its 21.5% 52-week gain versus XLU's 8% is a one-off deal re-rating, and the "27 mean-crossings / 46-day half-life" in my thesis is measured over a window that is majority pre-announcement and therefore no longer predictive. My own mandate screen requires stationarity and <25% two-year drift; this pair no longer passes. It also had D reporting Q2 on 2026-07-31, an event on a short I no longer want. EXITED both legs.

WFC/BAC — thesis intact but with a real fundamental headwind I should acknowledge. WFC +5% over 12 months vs BAC +26%. BAC grew NII 9% to $15.9bn and Q1 EPS +25%; WFC grew EPS 15% but NIM compressed to 2.47% from 2.67% and it is described as having posted back-to-back subpar quarters. Offsetting: the asset cap is gone, management guides $50bn NII for 2026, consensus has WFC EPS +11% and +12.9% in 2026/27, WFC bought back $4.0bn in Q1 alone against a $263bn cap, and it is cheaper on every multiple. Crucially both reported on 2026-07-14, so the divergence event is behind us and the 2.6sd gap is now a post-event price, not an anticipation. Still my best pair; sized up.

TSM/KLAC — the binary cleared IN MY FAVOUR after my book was set. KLAC reported FQ4 on 2026-07-28 (rev $3.66bn, non-GAAP EPS $1.05 vs $1.00 consensus) and the stock fell ~5% on guidance concerns despite the beat. TSM reported 2026-07-16 with ~65% earnings growth, price hikes and a $520 street target, yet has underperformed the semi sector and fell five sessions in a row into 07-28. Earnings risk on both legs is now spent. Increased, but kept the smallest sector pair because the 2.15/2.70 betas make it the most violent spread in the book.

LOW/HD — no structural break. Housing is bad for both (Ellison: "most difficult housing market since the financial crisis", 30y mortgage 6.53%, lowest turnover in years), HD hit a 52-week low in May and LOW in June. Consensus commentary favours LOW on execution across Pro and DIY. Both report mid-August, so no near-term event. Best hedge in the book (0.88 correlation); sized up.

MA/V — no structural break; stablecoin settlement and the AI-agent disintermediation debate hit both networks symmetrically (Mastercard added USDC/PYUSD/USDG/RLUSD settlement in June, Visa has run issuer settlement since 2021). Two things trimmed my enthusiasm: Visa already reported a clean beat (rev +17% y/y) and on 2026-07-28 announced 2,600 job cuts, a margin story that can defend V's premium; and MA reports pre-open TODAY (07-30), so any fill I get is post-print. This is also the lowest-payoff pair in the book — 4% spread vol means even full convergence is worth little per dollar of capital. Trimmed.

QUAL+IWF vs MTUM — thesis reinforced. MTUM is +29% YTD on the AI-chip surge, took its worst weekly loss of the year (~-7%) in the week ending 07-02, and its May/November rebalances mechanically rotate into whatever just worked. Multiple sources flag it as a concentrated bet on AI infrastructure. That is exactly the crowding premium I am short. Sized up modestly, with IWF larger than QUAL because IWF/MTUM is the wider dislocation (1.8sd vs 1.1sd).

  1. 2026-07-27OPENEDOpening book registered · experiments/round3/allocations/opus5_pairs.json

    Outlook at registrationThis book should look boring and should be judged on whether it makes money in flat or falling markets, not on whether it keeps up with SPY in a rally - realised volatility across four backtest windows was 2.5-3.8% annualised with drawdowns of 1-2.5% outside the in-sample window. Net SPY beta is +3.2% of NAV on 90% gross (49% long, 41% short, 10% cash), so market direction should contribute almost nothing either way; borrow on the 41% short side costs about 0.55% over five months and the 10% cash offsets roughly a sixth of that. Expected return is the convergence of six spreads - roughly +1.5 to +2.5% gross if they capture the historical third of their gap - which means fees and borrow are a material fraction of the edge and turnover must stay low. I have deliberately attached no stop-losses or take-profits: a standing order fires on one leg only, and a stopped-out short would leave a naked long and destroy the neutrality that is the entire point. Management is at the weekly reassessment instead: close any pair whose spread has reverted to within 0.25sd of its mean and redeploy into a newly stretched, still-stationary spread; cut any pair whose 250-day mean-crossing count collapses or whose two-year drift breaks past 25%, which is the signature of a re-rating rather than an oscillation; and re-check beta matching after any large relative move. The single biggest risk is the semis pair - if KLAC's run against TSM is a genuine re-rating of equipment over foundry, that 3% short can lose most of itself before the weekly review catches it.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-01-02 to 2025-06-30; 2024-01-03 to 2024-12-31
    strategy return pct2026H1 -6.78%; 2025H2 +1.62%; 2025H1 -1.48%; 2024 +5.96%
    benchmark return pct2026H1_SPY +8.74%; 2025H2_SPY +9.87%; 2025H1_SPY +6.31%; 2024_SPY +26.62%
    max drawdown pct2026H1 -8.11%; 2025H2 -1.1%; 2025H1 -2.54%; 2024 -1.48%

    Run through tracker/round2.py --backtest on this exact book. The 2026H1 number is not a forecast and is structurally in-sample-negative: the pairs were selected because their spreads widened during that very window, so replaying a static book across the divergence necessarily books the divergence as a loss. Almost all of it came from two legs - the KLAC short (KLAC +67% against TSM) and the MTUM short - which is exactly the gap the book is now being paid to fade. The genuinely out-of-sample windows are 2024 (entirely before the 250-day formation window) at +5.96% with a -1.48% drawdown, and 2025H1 at -1.48%; 2025H2 was +1.62% with a -1.10% drawdown. Second caveat: a static registered book cannot do what a real pairs strategy does - it cannot re-enter after convergence, rotate into newly stretched spreads, or exit a pair whose linkage has broken; the weekly reassessment is the only place that can happen. Third: an earlier draft included MSTR/COIN, ETH/BTC and CRWD/DDOG; all three were cut after the pooled event study showed the most extreme, highest-spread-volatility divergences (convergence >25%, spread vol >15%) historically kept widening (mean -4.7% to -9.2% over the next 110 sessions) rather than converging, and the ETH/BTC and LTC/BTC ratios failed the drift test outright (-41% to -59% over two years). Fourth: the pooled base rate for the surviving signal is modest - a spread at z<-1.25 returned about +1 to +6% over 110 sessions depending on bucket, so on ~7% average pair notional the honest expectation for this book is low single digits, not a large number.

  2. 2026-07-31REBALANCEUnrestricted-retail resize (position caps lifted, free-internet research poll) · experiments/desk/unrestricted_resize_2026-07-30.json
    Stated reason (desk log)

    Two changes, both driven by information rather than by the new freedom for its own sake. First, I am exiting the XLU/D pair entirely. NextEra's all-stock acquisition of Dominion at a fixed 0.8138 exchange ratio, announced 2026-05-18 with state review beginning 2026-07-16, means D is now priced off a deal ratio and a merger spread rather than off the utility sector. The stationarity that earned that pair its 16% of gross - 27 mean-crossings, 46-day half-life - is an artefact of a lookback window that is mostly pre-announcement. It fails my own screen's drift and stationarity tests going forward, and it carried a 07-31 earnings event on the short leg. A pairs mandate is a bet on spreads that revert; this one has been converted into a merger-arb position I did not choose and do not want. Second, having freed that capital and with all concentration caps gone, I am pushing gross from 90% to the full 100% and redistributing across the five surviving pairs in proportion to conviction rather than in near-equal slices. WFC/BAC goes from 20% to 34.8% of gross - it is the widest spread (2.6sd, 14% to convergence), has the tightest hedge economics (betas 0.76 vs 0.77, so it is dollar-neutral and beta-neutral simultaneously), 17 mean-crossings and near-zero two-year drift, and its divergence event (07-14 earnings) is now behind it. I am deliberately not going further than that: WFC's NIM compression to 2.47% and two subpar quarters are a genuine fundamental reason the spread widened, and a 2.6sd gap with a story attached is exactly the kind that can widen to 3.5sd before it reverts. LOW/HD rises to 21.5% because it is the cleanest hedge I own (0.88 correlation, betas 0.65/0.68) with no event until mid-August. The QUAL+IWF vs MTUM triangle rises to 19.3% with IWF weighted above QUAL, since MTUM's +29% YTD on AI chips and its worst week of the year in early July are exactly the crowding decay I am positioned for. TSM/KLAC rises to 12.4% - larger, because KLAC's 07-28 print resolved the way I wanted (beat, but -5% on guidance) and both legs' earnings risk is now spent, but still the smallest sector pair because 2.15/2.70 betas make it the most dangerous spread I hold. MA/V is trimmed to 12.0%: it is the most stationary spread in the screen but only 4% spread vol, so it is the least productive use of scarce gross, and Visa's 2,600-job cost-cut announcement on 07-28 gives the short leg a margin story that can defend its premium. I am attaching no stop-losses or take-profits anywhere. On a beta-matched pairs book a stop on one leg converts a hedged spread into a naked directional position at precisely the moment the spread is widest - which for a mean-reversion strategy is when expected return is highest, not lowest. Standing orders would systematically monetise my worst entries and destroy the edge. Every pair remains individually beta-cancelled; removing XLU/D (whose 0.16 / -0.09 beta mismatch generated almost the entire prior +3.2% residual) leaves aggregate net SPY beta at roughly +0.07% of NAV, which is more faithful to the market-neutral mandate, not less. Turnover is about 48% of NAV at ~2bps a side, roughly a dime of cost against a book I expect to work over weeks. Cash goes to zero: 4% APY on idle cash is worth about 1bp a week, less than the reversion I expect from putting that capital into WFC/BAC.

  3. 2026-08-10REBALANCERegistered rebalance · experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-10/opus5_pairs.json
    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-10/opus5_pairs.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-08: One leg's thesis was falsified by new information and one leg now carries a dated binary, so I am cutting both and moving the gross to the two spreads whose evidence improved. The falsification: I sized the MTUM short on the claim that momentum's excess is a crowding premium rather than an earnings premium. Micron — MTUM's largest holding at 6.26% — just posted revenue up more than fourfold with gross margin going 39% to 84.9%, and targets were hiked to $1,500-$1,697. That is an earnings premium, and I do not short earnings inflections on a factor argument. Compounding it, the November reconstitution is reported to push MTUM's semiconductor weight materially higher and lift its beta toward Micron's ~2.2, which would break the beta-cancellation the mandate requires of a short leg I cannot re-hedge until then. I halve the triangle rather than exit it because the 1.8sd/1.1sd dislocation and the 14-16 mean-crossings still pass my screen — the size was wrong, not the sign. The binary: HD reports 2026-08-18 and LOW 2026-08-19, confirmed by HD's 08-04 release, and analyst upside on the two has converged to ~14% vs ~15%, so the qualitative LOW-execution edge no longer supports 21.5% of gross across a two-day event window; I cut it to 17.6% and keep it, because two identical retailers printing 24 hours apart is the convergence catalyst, not a reason to be flat. The 9.4% of freed gross goes where the dislocation actually widened: BAC printed a 52-week high at $63.97 this week while WFC sits 11% below its own with a 12.7x vs 14.6x multiple gap and a 14.6% vs 8.9% target gap, so the 2.6sd spread got cheaper, not more expensive; and TSM/KLAC now has a 28.6% vs 16.5% analyst-upside gap with firms cutting KLAC targets post-print. I leave 9.45% in cash deliberately — it earns 4% APY against zero spread risk, and I would rather bank that than force capital into MA/V, whose 4% spread vol I already judged the least productive use of gross. I am attaching no stops anywhere, on purpose: a stop on one leg of a beta-matched pair fills the short and leaves me naked long, which is precisely the failure mode that took out 12 of the 17 standing orders ever triggered in this experiment. In a pair book, size is the risk control, not price triggers.

    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-17/opus5_pairs.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two of my five spreads stopped qualifying this week for opposite reasons, and the reason I trimmed a third was erased by new information. MA/V hit its exit condition: MA rose 15% on a clean Q2 (net revenue +14%, adj EPS $5.04 vs $4.77, guidance raised) and the target-implied gap that got me in collapsed from 9 points to 2.6. A mandate built on stationary spreads takes the convergence when it arrives; holding on hoping a mean-reverting spread overshoots is not the trade I described, and MA's move was earnings, not noise, so I will not flip the sign either. The factor triangle goes to zero because I already conceded its thesis was falsified — I underwrote momentum's excess as crowding and MU/AMD/AVGO delivered earnings instead — and a residual short of a thesis I no longer believe is just a slow leak, which it proved again this week (MTUM +2.55% vs IWF +0.55%). The November reconstitution will also drag MTUM's beta toward Micron's ~2.2 against the ~1.5 my triangle is matched to, and I cannot re-hedge drift from inside a fund; better to own no beta mismatch than a small one I cannot fix. Against that I add to the two spreads whose evidence improved. WFC/BAC widened against me on price while widening in my favour on substance: BAC printed a fresh 52-week high at $65.20 and its consensus upside fell to 7.1% while WFC's held at 14.3%, so the convergence gap went from 5.7 to 7.2 points on the book's best stationarity evidence (17 mean-crossings, ~zero two-year drift, 0.80 correlation). LOW/HD is the honest reversal: last week I cut it from 21.5% of gross precisely because consensus upside had converged to ~14% vs ~15% and I refused to pay for a two-day earnings window with no edge in it. That gap is now 9.1 points (LOW +19.5% with the stock near its 52-week low, HD +10.4% on freshly RAISED targets), LOW's bar into the print is lower (EPS guided down yoy on deal costs), and HD's CEO is on medical leave. The condition that justified the trim is gone, so I restore the size rather than pretend consistency means never changing back. TSM/KLAC stays exactly where it is because the week cut both ways — Lam lifting CY2026 WFE to the low $150bns says the cycle peak is higher than my short assumed, while AMAT dropping 6% on record revenue and a 51% growth guide says the multiple, not the fundamentals, is the binding constraint. Mixed evidence is a reason to hold a position, not to resize it. Gross falls from 90.5% to 77.7% and cash rises to 22.3%: I cut two sub-books and found no replacement that passed my screen — XLU/D is now a merger-arb instrument because of the NextEra deal, CVX/XOM trade at identical forward multiples, GS/MS is a one-point gap — so the unused gross earns 4% instead of buying a spread I have not measured. I attach no stops or take-profits anywhere: on a beta-matched pair a per-leg percentage stop is triggered by the market's direction rather than the spread's, and firing one leg converts a hedged relative-value position into an outright directional bet, which is a worse outcome than the loss it was meant to cap. Everything fills at the next open — I want the MA/V convergence banked before it can give back, and the LOW/HD size on before the 08-18 print.

    Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Two of my three pairs delivered the thing I said I was waiting for, and my own stated exit rule says convergence gets taken rather than admired. TSM/KLAC moved about 40% of the modelled 19% convergence in a single week - one fifth of its 34-day half-life - and it did so while the fundamental case for the short eroded: KLAC guided fiscal Q1 revenue and profit above consensus, so the entire 10% fall was multiple compression from 55.7x to 50.3x. My short thesis was explicitly that 'the multiple is the binding constraint'; the multiple has now partly paid out, which makes the leg less attractive at exactly the moment it made money. I cut it by about 38% rather than closing because 6.3 points of target gap remain. LOW/HD is a different problem: the reason I carried it at full size was a specific pre-print asymmetry, and the print is over. Worse, the execution difference I claimed to be buying arrived and pointed the wrong way - HD comped +1.7% and reaffirmed, LOW comped +0.2%, missed revenue and cut FY guidance to the bottom end - so my long leg's de-rating now has a cause rather than being noise. The gap that got me in halved from 9.1 to 5.3 points. I keep half the pair because 5.2 turns of multiple and 5.3 points of target gap still favour LOW, the hedge quality is the second-best I own, and both names are now a clear quarter away from any catalyst. The freed capital goes partly into WFC/BAC and mostly into cash. I add to the bank pair for the same reason I added last week and for no other: the measure I actually underwrote got more stretched, from a 7.2-point target gap to 8.1, and the year-to-date split is now BAC +15% against WFC -8% in a spread with 0.80 correlation and near-zero two-year drift. The Berkshire sale of another $1.6bn of BAC is new evidence on the short leg. I add moderately rather than to the hilt because this pair is now about two-thirds of gross; I accept that ratio only because gross itself is down to 66% and every leg is beta-cancelled, so the absolute risk of the concentration is small. I leave 33.6% in cash at 4% rather than force a sixth pair: XLU/D is disqualified by NextEra's $66.8bn bid for Dominion, which replaces mean reversion with deal probability, and the QUAL+IWF vs MTUM factor spread has already reverted 12% before I would have entered. Carrying no stops remains deliberate - stopping one side of a beta-matched pair leaves the other side naked directional, which is the failure mode this mandate exists to avoid.

    Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Two things force my hand and they point the same way. First, my own audited rule: convergence gets taken rather than admired. WFC/BAC closed 35% of its target-gap in a single week, 8.1 points to 5.28 - that is the same trigger, at the same magnitude, that made me cut TSM/KLAC last week at 40% captured. If I book profit on a pair that works and hold full size on the one that works better, the rule is decoration. So WFC comes 23.0 to 19.0 and BAC 22.7 to 18.7, trimmed in beta-proportion so the cut does not quietly leave a directional bank bet. Second, concentration: WFC/BAC was 69% of gross, which meant I owned one spread wearing a diversified book's clothing. The trim plus a fourth pair takes it to 52% of gross and my largest single leg from 23% to 19%. I am not doing this to be smaller - gross rises 66.4% to 72.9% - I am doing it to be less singular. Where the money goes is long MA / short V, a pair from my original screen that I sized at zero because the spread was not stretched then and now is: MA has trailed V by 8.3 points over a year and the traditional 3-5 turn Mastercard multiple premium has gone to zero, while MA still compounds EPS at 22% against V's 10% and carries an order of magnitude less interchange-litigation provision. LOW/HD and TSM/KLAC hold. On LOW/HD specifically I am neither adding nor cutting, and I want the reason on the record: the spread widened against me on a rate shock, not on news, and everything I underwrote got cheaper - 7.9 points of target gap versus 5.3, a 5.5-turn discount, 9% versus 5% consensus growth. A mean-reversion mandate would normally add there. I do not, because I halved this pair a week ago on a fundamental point that has not been retracted - LOW guided to the bottom end while HD reaffirmed - and adding into a stretch I myself argued was fundamentally deserved would be doubling down against my own stated read. Holding is the honest position between those two facts. I carry no stops anywhere, unchanged and deliberate: a stop on one leg of a beta-matched pair does not reduce risk, it converts a spread into a naked directional position at the worst possible moment. Net SPY beta lands at about +0.06% of NAV rather than the mandate's +3.2%; with September hike odds at 55% I would rather run flatter than my brief than tilt long into it, and I state the deviation rather than bury it.

    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-09-08/opus5_pairs.json

    Two things changed this week, and together they force a full replacement rather than a hold. FIRST, I re-ran my own screen on my own live book and it failed. Of the four pairs I am actually carrying, not one would pass a fresh application of my mandate's stationarity test today: WFC/BAC has crossed its 250-day spread mean exactly ONCE in the past year with a 91-day half-life (my rule requires 8 crossings) - it is a trend I have been calling a spread, and the +2.9% it has made me is drift, not convergence; MA/V is at z -0.96 with 3 crossings; LOW/HD is at z +1.03 with 6 crossings; and KLAC/TSM has fully converged to z -0.13, so there is no edge left in it at all - it is the leg that cost me -5.79% on the KLAC short. A book with zero remaining signal and zero remaining stationarity is not something to hold out of thrift; the 2bps-per-side cost of turning it over is trivially cheaper than carrying four dead positions for another week. SECOND, and more important, I found out WHY my single-stock pairs kept breaking. I ran the statistical screen first and then checked the news on every finalist, and the news killed almost the entire statistical leaderboard: CRM/SAP (z 2.71, the top-ranked pair in the whole screen) - Salesforce beat and RAISED on Sep 1 with Cantor, TD Cowen and Argus all taking targets to $300; IHI/MDT (z -2.78) - Medtronic beat and raised Sep 1 with 13.7% organic growth and Mizuho/UBS/BofA target hikes; NTRS/STT (z -2.23) - State Street's Q2 profit was up 56%, it raised 2026 guidance and is buying Santander's LatAm custody business; KEY/USB (z -2.14) - U.S. Bancorp posted record revenue, upgraded guidance and is monetising the BTIG deal; COP/DVN and COP/XOM (z 2.15/2.04) - ConocoPhillips beat, hit its $5B divestiture target early and drew target raises from six firms; DHR/TMO (z -2.35) - Danaher cut its revenue outlook in July, had its worst day in two decades and changed CEO on Aug 3; AXP/COF - Capital One is re-rating on Discover synergies. Every one of those was me being asked to short a company that had just beaten and raised, or to buy one that had just guided down. That is the exact error that cost me on KLAC, and it is not a statistical error - the z-score cannot see it. This is a fundamentals-driven dispersion regime, and in one of those, single-name convergence trades are systematically adversely selected. So the book is rebuilt around a rule the old one did not have: four of five pairs are now ETF-vs-ETF or sector-vs-broad-index, where no single earnings report can permanently break the spread, and the one surviving single-name pair (STLD/NUE) is a business-identical twin pair where I verified that BOTH legs are driven by the SAME catalyst (the U.S.-Canada trade breakdown pushing steel tariffs) and neither has a divergent fundamental. I also deliberately declined the three highest 'annualised edge' names the screen produced - NEM/XME, NEM/SLV and GDX/GLD - because their 60-day spread momentum is +0.19 to +0.29 and still accelerating: gold miners are in a parabolic move and fading a parabola is the KLAC mistake in a different costume. I dropped the energy pair (EOG/XOP, z -2.17) for the same class of reason: XOP is up 49% on the year on an active U.S.-Iran conflict and Hormuz supply risk with crude testing $90, and I have no edge on a shooting war. Two structural changes beyond selection. (1) Gross exposure goes from 72.9% to 90% and cash from 27.1% to 10%. The old book's realised risk was absurdly low - max drawdown of 0.71% over seven weeks - because I was running a quarter of the book in cash on top of pairs that barely moved. The new book's measured spread volatility is 3.4% annualised with a pairwise correlation matrix that is near-zero everywhere except one 0.61 (XLI/VTV vs ITA/RSP, which share a long-cyclicals leg and which I accept as the book's single concentration). At that level of volatility, holding 27% cash to earn 4% is not prudence, it is under-deployment. (2) I am running no stop-losses or take-profits anywhere, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. Stops here are evaluated per LEG against entry fill, so a stop firing on one side of a pair converts a hedged spread into a naked directional position - it makes the book strictly more dangerous at exactly the moment it is losing. In a market-neutral pairs book the risk control has to live in pair selection, half-life and sizing, which is where I have put it. Beta discipline is unchanged and verified two ways: the sum of beta-weighted legs and an independent 250-day regression of the assembled book's daily P&L on SPY both give +3.0% of NAV per 1% SPY move, against my +3.2% mandate. The book is net -8.8% in dollars and +3.0% in beta, which is the correct shape when the short legs are low-beta value baskets.

    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-09-16/opus5_pairs.json

    Five supposedly independent pairs lost money in the same week, in the same direction, on all five: every long leg fell (XLI -2.63, ITA -3.25, MTUM -2.56, STLD -1.50, IJR -2.69) and every short leg rose. Under genuine independence that is a roughly 1-in-32 outcome per direction, and I am treating it as evidence rather than noise: the book was not five uncorrelated stationary spreads, it was one factor bet - long cyclical/small/high-beta/momentum, short defensive-value - that happened to net to +3.0% SPY beta. Cancelling SPY beta cancelled the wrong thing. The factor that actually bit is rates and duration, and it bit because the regime changed underneath the screen. The 250-day lookback that measured these spreads covers a Fed that was on hold after cutting; as of this week the 10-year printed 5.00% (highest since October 2023), WTI is $101.39 on Saudi pipeline disruption, and roughly 90% of the market expects Chair Warsh to HIKE 25bp on 2026-09-16. Stationarity is an assumption about an unchanged regime, and the regime changed. My mandate already contains the governing rule - remove every pair whose dislocation was caused by a fresh fundamental catalyst on the leg being faded - so I am re-running that hand-filter with this week's information rather than abandoning mean reversion. It disqualifies three pairs. IJR/IWD: a 10-year through 5% and a hiking Fed is THE fundamental cause of small-cap cheapness versus large value (floating-rate debt, refi cost); the Russell 2000 underperformed again on 9/14. That pair was never a spread, it was a duration bet with two tickers. MTUM/XLK: the 9/14 shock was Amodei, Altman and Musk publicly calling for slower AI development, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -5.9% on the week; MTUM's current constituent set is far more semis/AI-power heavy than XLK's software-weighted book, so I was long the exact leg a brand-new, unresolved regulatory and sentiment catalyst is hitting. ITA/RSP: ITA is -9.8% from its 14 August pivot top on a confirmed technical sell signal, and at 22% GE / 17% RTX / 9% BA three names drive the whole ETF - that is a trend in a concentrated basket, not a stationary dislocation, and equal-weight RSP is not a factor-match for it. One point that does NOT favour holding: exit and entry both fill at the 2026-09-16 close, which is after the 2pm decision, so I carry FOMC-day risk on the old book either way. Holding versus trading changes nothing about tomorrow and everything about the weeks after, and I do not want to own long-cyclical/small/momentum versus short-defensive-value into a post-hike tape. The cost of acting is trivial: about 74% of notional turns over at 2bps plus SEC/TAF, roughly 1.5bps of NAV, against a book that has given back 0.61% on this leg. What I am NOT doing is replacing the three dropped pairs with new ones. My edge is a measured 250-day z-score plus stationarity screen over 3,000 pairs, and I cannot re-run that screen in this session; substituting five intuition-picked pairs with invented z-scores would discard the only thing that makes this book a strategy rather than a narrative. So the honest posture is concentration into what still passes plus 40% cash at 4% APY until the screen can be re-run on post-hike data. I have also added stops for the first time, but only on the two single-name legs where idiosyncratic blow-up risk is real - a stop on a diversified ETF leg would only ever fire in a market event, which is precisely when I want the hedge intact.

Research notes — free-internet poll, desk run 2026-07-30

Researched the July 28-29 FOMC and the tape since my 7/27 book was set. Findings: (1) Fed held at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth meeting but THREE members dissented in favour of a 25bp HIKE; markets now price roughly 60-79% odds of at least one hike by the September meeting. Long-dated yields rose on the announcement — a bear steepener, not a bull flattener. (2) Risk assets sold off hard on 7/29: S&P -1.52% to 7,316, Dow -2.19% (-1,100pts), Nasdaq -1.74%, with the Nasdaq 100 entering correction. (3) The proximate equity story is AI-capex skepticism, not rates alone: Meta missed by $1.04 (EPS $6.18), expenses +55% to $42bn vs revenue +28%, net income -14%, and guided Q3 light — shares -6% to -10% after hours. Microsoft beat (rev $90.01bn vs $87.62bn est, Azure +43% cc) and rose ~2.4%. SK Hynix disappointed and semis were the worst group. (4) Geopolitics: Iran launched an attempted surprise attack, the first US-Iran re-engagement since the recent pause; Brent jumped over 7% through $90, a seven-month high. Energy and utilities were the only groups showing positive breadth. (5) Inflation is 3.5% headline / 2.6% core and cooling, but a $90+ oil impulse plus three hike dissents means the disinflation trade is over. (6) Gold sits at $4,066, far below the January $5,595 peak, and notably ROSE 0.94% on the hawkish day when yields rose — a resilience tell and cleaner positioning. (7) XLU has 90% of constituents above their 200-day EMA, the highest breadth of any of the 11 sectors, driven by AI power demand rather than by duration. (8) DXY is rangebound near 101, not breaking out, which weakens the dollar-strength half of my EFA-short case.

How this maps onto my measured seasonal windows: the macro regime AGREES with my highest-conviction stats (short IEF, long XLI, long XLF/KRE — a bear steepener is the single best backdrop for bank NIM, and industrials carry my strongest measured window at 81% hit rate and t=+2.49/+3.78) and FIGHTS my weakest stat (QQQ minus SPY was only t=+1.35, the least significant number in my entire study, and it now sits against a correction, an AI-capex de-rating and rising discount rates). Gold's Aug-Sep restocking window is reinforced by a live shooting war and an oil-driven inflation impulse. Utilities' rate sensitivity is offset by best-in-market breadth and a structural power-demand bid.

Management is calendar-scheduled rather than discretionary, using the weekly Friday reassessments. Around Sep-30 I intend to deploy the 7% cash into a BTC leg for the measured Uptober window (9/11 years, avg +19.4%, t=+3.60) with a stop, and to add to XLU, whose Sep-30-to-Oct-31 window is 19/26 years positive. Around Oct-31 I rotate the QQQ overweight toward mid/small caps for the Nov-Dec leg, where MDY minus SPY is +1.18% at t=+2.27 and IWM minus SPY is +1.42% at t=+1.67 while QQQ minus SPY is actually negative (10/26 years), and I add XRT for the holiday build (+3.80% avg, 13/20 years, and 7/10 in the last decade at +7.38%). I cover the IEF short if the Nov-Dec equity-over-duration spread has already paid, and I will cover EFA early if it outperforms SPY by more than 3% over any four-week stretch, since that is the direct falsifier of the leg. Within each month I bias any incremental buying to the turn-of-the-month window (last trading day through the third trading day, +0.263% average, 57% hit over 318 months) rather than mid-month. The risk I am carrying knowingly is that this is a screened-winner book with one observation per year per effect, so I will size down rather than double down if the Aug-Oct leg does not behave.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-07-28 to 2025-10-31; 2024-07-29 to 2024-10-31

    max drawdown pct2026H1 -7.21%; 2025H2 -3.39%; 2025_seasonal_AugOct -2.03%; 2024_seasonal_AugOct -4.1%

    MULTIPLE TESTING IS THE MAIN CAVEAT AND I AM REPORTING SCREENED WINNERS. I screened 36 instruments across 5 calendar windows on an absolute basis, the same 36 relative to SPY, 24 explicit long/short spreads across 3 windows, plus turn-of-the-month and crypto calendar variants — well over 400 statistics. At 400 tests one expects several 70%+ hit rates by chance alone, and none of the reported t-statistics would survive a Bonferroni correction. That is why every position is quoted with its hit-rate and n rather than an average alone, and why I preferred effects that hold on BOTH the full sample and the last 10 years and have an economic flow story, over the higher-average but lower-hit-rate tail-driven ones (OIH -4.6% avg but only 36% hit; USO -9.9% avg but heavily contaminated by futures roll decay rather than seasonality). SAMPLE SIZE: the longest series give n=26 non-overlapping years, several (KRE, IEF, GLD) give only n=20-23, and the crypto statistic is n=11; a 21/26 hit rate has a one-sided binomial p of about 0.005 but is one observation per year, so the effective sample is tiny. WINDOW OVERLAP: Jul27-Sep30, Jul27-Oct31 and Jul27-Dec31 are nested, so their statistics are not independent evidence. HONEST NEGATIVE FINDINGS: (1) the famous 'August/September weakness' is NOT a directional edge — SPY was positive in 14/26 Aug-31-to-Sep-30 windows with a median of +0.30%; the negative -1.20% average is produced entirely by tail years (2001, 2002, 2008, 2022), so the correct trade is lower drawdown, not a short. (2) The seasonal window ahead is net POSITIVE (SPY Jul-27 to Dec-31 avg +3.90%, 19/26 years, t=+2.09), which is why this book is net long ~75% rather than market-neutral. (3) The book's measured edge is a higher hit rate (17/20 positive years vs SPY 19/26) and roughly 70% of SPY's drawdown, NOT reliable outperformance: it beat SPY in only 7/20 Jul-Dec windows and 11/20 Aug-Oct windows, and it lagged SPY in 3 of the 4 engine backtests above. In a strong bull tape this construction will underperform, and the recorded backtests show exactly that. ENGINE-SPECIFIC: shorts consume weight budget in this engine, so net exposure is capped at long-minus-short; the KRE stop is set at -25% and did not trigger in any of the four windows; an earlier candidate that shorted OIH was stopped out in both mandatory windows and was discarded, and an earlier candidate holding 4-5% BTC at entry underperformed this one in 3 of 4 windows, consistent with the measured BTC Aug-Sep statistic. All backtest figures above are verbatim from tracker/round2.py --backtest.

    CUT QQQ 20 -> 6. This was my largest position and my weakest evidence: QQQ minus SPY measured t=+1.35, the least significant statistic in my entire study, and I was carrying it at top weight purely because it was the 'growth core'. It now faces three simultaneous headwinds — the Nasdaq 100 is in correction, Meta missed by $1.04 with expenses +55% against revenue +28% and guided Q3 light, and rising long yields compress exactly this duration. I keep a 6% stub because QQQ's ABSOLUTE Jul-27 to Dec-31 window is still +3.97% at 20/26 years (77%) and Microsoft's Azure +43% shows the capex is at least buying revenue; it is the relative-to-SPY case, not the absolute case, that was thin. Sizing by measured conviction is the mandate, and this leg measured worst.

    SIZE UP IEF SHORT 4 -> 17. This is now the single cleanest idea I own. My seasonal read was already the most extreme number in the study — intermediate Treasuries beat SPY in only 5/23 years (22%) over this window and in just 1 of the last 10, at -6.00% average. The macro has now arrived at the same conclusion from the other side: three FOMC dissents for a hike, ~60-79% odds of a hike by September, a $90 Brent inflation impulse, and long yields that ROSE on a hold. At 4% this leg could not earn anything even if it was perfectly right. At 17% it can. 3% borrow over five months costs ~0.2% of NAV, which is cheap for the only leg that pays off in the scenario that hurts everything else I own.

    SIZE UP XLI 18 -> 20 and XLF 13 -> 16, KRE 6 -> 7. These carry my best measured windows (XLI +5.39%, 21/26 years, t=+2.49, with Nov-Dec at t=+3.78 and t=+3.04 versus SPY; XLF +5.04% at 20/26 and 9/10 in the last decade at +8.94%; KRE the highest-return sleeve at +7.24%, t=+2.28, 8/10 last decade at +10.14%). Crucially the macro now reinforces rather than merely permits them: a bear steepener with the Fed on hold and long yields rising is the textbook environment for bank net interest margin, and industrials are the cyclical least exposed to the AI-capex de-rating while benefiting from defense spending in an active Middle East conflict. Financials and industrials were both named in the broad-participation breadth data.

    SIZE UP GLD 13 -> 15. My cleanest non-equity seasonal (+3.54% Jul-27 to Oct-27, t=+1.69, +3.13% versus SPY at t=+1.80) now has a live geopolitical and inflation catalyst stacked on top, and the tell that matters is that gold rose 0.94% on the hawkish day while yields rose. Positioning is also far cleaner at $4,066 than at the January $5,595 peak. This is simultaneously my seasonal leg and the hedge that pays if the September hike breaks my cyclical longs.

    HOLD XLU 9 -> 8. I expected to cut this as a bond proxy into a hiking scare, but the breadth data argued me out of it: 90% of XLU constituents sit above their 200-day EMA, the strongest of all 11 sectors, because the bid is AI power demand rather than duration. Combined with a positive measured Sep-30 to Oct-31 window (19/26 years, 8/10 in the last decade) I keep it near full size, trimming a point for rate risk.

    DROP XLP 5 -> 0. Painful because it had my highest t-statistic (t=+3.32 absolute, t=+3.93 for Nov-Dec), but that edge is concentrated in the Oct-31 to Dec-31 leg, and staples face input-cost compression from a $90 oil shock in the meantime. This is a timing decision, not a rejection: I intend to re-enter it with cash at the November rotation, which is exactly what the dry powder is for.

    TRIM EFA SHORT 5 -> 5 (unchanged). I nearly cut this. The seasonal case is genuinely good (positive in only 9/24 years, 2/10 in the last decade at -2.65%), but half of its mechanism was dollar strength and DXY is stuck near 101 rather than breaking out — and a US-led tech correction can actually flatter less tech-heavy foreign indices. Holding at existing size rather than adding, since its natural pair (long QQQ) just shrank by two thirds.

    CASH 7 -> 6. I release one point to fund the IEF short while preserving essentially all pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 and Nov-1 rotations, when XLP and the mid/small-cap shift come back on.

    Standing orders: I tighten KRE's stop from -25% to -20%, because the original -25% was calibrated to the 2008 drawdown as a pure beta event, whereas the live risk is credit stress from a hike landing on top of an oil shock, which would show up faster. I add a -18% stop on the QQQ stub and a -12% stop on EFA. I attach a -10% stop to the IEF short: if intermediate Treasuries rally 10% against me that is a flight-to-quality recession event, in which case my industrials, financials and regional banks are all bleeding too and I want that leg closed rather than doubling the correlation. I put a +30% take-profit on GLD to bank an extreme war spike, set deliberately wide so it does not decapitate the hedge during ordinary strength. Taking the next available fill rather than naming a date — I am adding to cyclicals into a flush, which is the right side of this print, and waiting for a bounce to sell my QQQ cut would be over-cleverness.

At 17% it can. 3% borrow over five months costs ~0.2% of NAV, which is cheap for the only leg that pays off in the scenario that hurts everything else I own.

    SIZE UP XLI 18 -> 20 and XLF 13 -> 16, KRE 6 -> 7. These carry my best measured windows (XLI +5.39%, 21/26 years, t=+2.49, with Nov-Dec at t=+3.78 and t=+3.04 versus SPY; XLF +5.04% at 20/26 and 9/10 in the last decade at +8.94%; KRE the highest-return sleeve at +7.24%, t=+2.28, 8/10 last decade at +10.14%). Crucially the macro now reinforces rather than merely permits them: a bear steepener with the Fed on hold and long yields rising is the textbook environment for bank net interest margin, and industrials are the cyclical least exposed to the AI-capex de-rating while benefiting from defense spending in an active Middle East conflict. Financials and industrials were both named in the broad-participation breadth data.

    SIZE UP GLD 13 -> 15. My cleanest non-equity seasonal (+3.54% Jul-27 to Oct-27, t=+1.69, +3.13% versus SPY at t=+1.80) now has a live geopolitical and inflation catalyst stacked on top, and the tell that matters is that gold rose 0.94% on the hawkish day while yields rose. Positioning is also far cleaner at $4,066 than at the January $5,595 peak. This is simultaneously my seasonal leg and the hedge that pays if the September hike breaks my cyclical longs.

    HOLD XLU 9 -> 8. I expected to cut this as a bond proxy into a hiking scare, but the breadth data argued me out of it: 90% of XLU constituents sit above their 200-day EMA, the strongest of all 11 sectors, because the bid is AI power demand rather than duration. Combined with a positive measured Sep-30 to Oct-31 window (19/26 years, 8/10 in the last decade) I keep it near full size, trimming a point for rate risk.

    DROP XLP 5 -> 0. Painful because it had my highest t-statistic (t=+3.32 absolute, t=+3.93 for Nov-Dec), but that edge is concentrated in the Oct-31 to Dec-31 leg, and staples face input-cost compression from a $90 oil shock in the meantime. This is a timing decision, not a rejection: I intend to re-enter it with cash at the November rotation, which is exactly what the dry powder is for.

    TRIM EFA SHORT 5 -> 5 (unchanged). I nearly cut this. The seasonal case is genuinely good (positive in only 9/24 years, 2/10 in the last decade at -2.65%), but half of its mechanism was dollar strength and DXY is stuck near 101 rather than breaking out — and a US-led tech correction can actually flatter less tech-heavy foreign indices. Holding at existing size rather than adding, since its natural pair (long QQQ) just shrank by two thirds.

    CASH 7 -> 6. I release one point to fund the IEF short while preserving essentially all pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 and Nov-1 rotations, when XLP and the mid/small-cap shift come back on.

    Standing orders: I tighten KRE's stop from -25% to -20%, because the original -25% was calibrated to the 2008 drawdown as a pure beta event, whereas the live risk is credit stress from a hike landing on top of an oil shock, which would show up faster. I add a -18% stop on the QQQ stub and a -12% stop on EFA. I attach a -10% stop to the IEF short: if intermediate Treasuries rally 10% against me that is a flight-to-quality recession event, in which case my industrials, financials and regional banks are all bleeding too and I want that leg closed rather than doubling the correlation. I put a +30% take-profit on GLD to bank an extreme war spike, set deliberately wide so it does not decapitate the hedge during ordinary strength. Taking the next available fill rather than naming a date — I am adding to cyclicals into a flush, which is the right side of this print, and waiting for a bounce to sell my QQQ cut would be over-cleverness.

    Two things changed and they point the same direction. (1) The calendar moved. My strategy of record was sized off a Jul-27-to-year-end window; that window is now half spent and what remains is front-loaded with the single worst stretch in the sample. Sep 8 through roughly Oct 10 is the weakest four weeks of the S&P year, and in midterm years specifically the autumn low arrives EARLY - late September or early October - before the Q4 lift. JP Morgan's midterm quarterly series (Q1 -0.5%, Q2 -0.6%, Q3 -0.1%, Q4 +6.6%) and the +13.59% mean midterm run from the autumn low to year-end are both rallies I want to own, but they start AFTER the window I am about to trade through, not during it. The 2026 caveat is real too: the index is already +12.78% YTD, so the setup the midterm pattern normally requires (three weak quarters) has not occurred, which argues for buying the pattern later and cheaper rather than paying up for it now. (2) The macro catalyst calendar now agrees with the seasonal calendar for once. August payrolls printed 162k against 53k expected with June and July revised up, the 2-year yield broke to its highest since January 2025, core CPI is running 3.0% on a 3m annualized basis and core PCE 3.7% on top of the Hormuz energy shock, Chair Warsh has said the Fed has 'work to do' on prices, three FOMC members already dissented for a hike in July, and September hike odds are ~50-66% with BofA looking for hikes in September, October and December. A Fed hiking into the seasonal air pocket is exactly the configuration in which the historical September drawdown gets realised rather than faded. So I am cutting gross from 86% to 73% and raising cash from 14% to 27%, which is the dry powder the strategy of record explicitly pre-committed to the Oct-1 rotation. Three specific leg changes. QQQ goes from 22% to 10%: long-duration megacap growth at ~29x forward is the single leg most exposed to a hike into hot core inflation, and mid-September to mid-October is the Nasdaq's own weakest window - I keep 10% rather than zero because Q4 tech seasonality is genuinely strong and I do not want to be flat if Waller's dovish wing wins and the hike gets priced out. KRE goes to zero: hikes squeeze regional-bank NIM because funding costs reprice ahead of assets, KRE has diverged from XLF by the widest margin since the SVB episode, and it was my highest-beta equity leg heading into the weakest calendar window; XLF is the cleaner and cheaper expression of the same Q4 financials seasonal. EFA short goes to zero: the measured Aug-Dec statistic that developed non-US lags the S&P is real in the 2000-2025 sample, but the live regime has run flat against it - EFA beat the S&P 31.6% to 17.7% in 2025 and is still ahead in 2026 even in dollar terms on valuation (19x vs 29x), German fiscal stimulus and dollar softness - and the leg is already -0.84%. A seasonal edge worth tens of basis points is not worth paying 3% borrow to fight a two-year relative trend. I accept that this book will lag if the market simply melts up; the mandate is to be paid in the Oct-Dec window, and I would rather enter that window with 27% cash and no forced sellers in the book than defend an 86% gross position through the four weeks the data says to avoid.

    The macro half of my two-filter rule inverted between 2026-09-08 and now, so five of six legs had to be re-tested even though the calendar half is unchanged. On 2026-09-08 I built this leg expecting a Fed on hold into a seasonally weak tape. As of 2026-09-15 the market prices roughly a 90% chance the FOMC HIKES 25bp on 2026-09-16 after August CPI accelerated, with WTI near $105 on the ongoing US-Iran conflict and the 10y at its highest since 2007; the 1-month WTI/10y correlation is ~0.96, the tightest since 2019, so oil and yields are now a single shock rather than two. The seasonal statistic itself is being confirmed in real time, not contradicted: the S&P closed 7,621.54 on 2026-09-14, down again, exactly in the Sep-8-to-early-Oct window that midterm-year data says is the worst four weeks of the cycle, and the payoff for that patience is the Q4 midterm-year record (up 86% of years since 1940, +6.6% average) that my cash is reserved for. So the calendar call is to reduce gross further and hold more dry powder, not to spend it. Concretely: gross falls 73% to 54% and cash rises 27% to 46%. XLU long is killed and re-expressed as a SHORT (it was the worst leg in the book at -3.91% and is trading as a pure bond proxy into a hike). XLI long is killed outright ($105 oil is a direct input-cost hit to industrials and the rate shock compounds it). QQQ long is killed (chips reeling on the AI-slowdown call plus a rising discount rate is the worst possible combination in the worst seasonal window, and buying megacap beta back cheaper on Oct 1 is precisely what the cash is for). IEF short is upsized from 14% to 18% as the single leg where seasonal (September is historically the worst month for Treasuries) and catalyst (hiking Fed, accelerating CPI, oil-linked yields) agree without qualification. XLF is kept but cut 15% to 12% (higher-for-longer helps NIM and financials carry the strongest cyclical Q4 seasonality, but a hike into a stagflationary shock adds credit risk). GLD is cut 12% to 8%: its two drivers now disagree, war and inflation support it while rising real yields and a firmer dollar have already pulled it off its January record to ~$4,275, and my rule says a leg with a split signal gets carried small, not at full size. XLE is added at 9% as the only sector where the shock is a tailwind and as the explicit hedge on the escalation tail that would hurt everything else here. Turnover cost is a few basis points at 2bps per side, which is cheap relative to carrying three legs that are now positioned against the Wednesday catalyst.

At 10% it is also the leg that protects me against the most plausible way this book is wrong — the hike being fully priced and equities rallying in relief once the uncertainty clears at 2pm on entry day. Entry is at the 2026-09-16 close, after the decision and dot plot are public, so this fill already reflects the outcome.

  1. 2026-07-27OPENEDOpening book registered · experiments/round3/allocations/opus5_trend.json

    Outlook at registrationExpect a low-beta, low-drawdown return stream that looks nothing like the index: net equity exposure is only about +38% gross long minus 8% short, and roughly half the risk budget sits in currency (EUO), agriculture (DBA), energy (XLE/USO) and the short metals/crypto sleeve. In a continuation regime the dollar, financials, healthcare and energy legs compound while the metals and crypto shorts pay a second time; in a chop regime both sides bleed at once and the wide stops mean the book gives back slowly rather than crashing. Management plan: re-sign every market at each Friday reassessment on the same two filters (price vs 200dma AND 3-month time-series momentum), flip or flatten any leg whose filters disagree, re-scale weights to 60-day inverse vol, and cut the whole book toward cash if fewer than half the universe shows a coherent trend. The specific things I will watch are gold reclaiming its 50dma (would flatten GLD/SLV), BTC closing back above its 200dma (would cover the perp), and XLK/SOXL basing - if tech re-accelerates while XLY stays weak the short-discretionary leg becomes the wrong hedge.
